prompt: Draw an architecture diagram of a checkout request path: a web app calls a Checkout API, which writes to a Postgres Orders DB and charges cards through an external Payment provider. Put the API and the DB inside a group called Private VPC.

Draw a flowchart of a password reset: start, enter email, decision 'Account exists?', if yes send a reset link and wait for the click, then verify the token and end with 'Password changed'; if no go back to entering the email.

Draw a flowchart of a release gate: start, run tests, decision 'Tests pass?' (no: fix and rerun), manual approval step, deploy to staging, decision 'Smoke test ok?' (no: roll back), deploy to production, end.

Draw a sequence diagram of a login: the user sends credentials to the app, the app asks the Auth API to verify them, the Auth API looks the user up in the Users DB, then returns a token which the app stores. Wrap the lookup and the token in an 'opt' frame labelled 'user found'.

Draw a sequence diagram of a payment with retry: the shopper presses Pay, the web app calls the Orders service, which charges the Payment provider; the provider declines, Orders schedules a retry on itself, charges again and the provider approves. Use a loop frame around the charge attempts.
Draw a state diagram of an order lifecycle: start, Placed, Paid, a choice 'Stock ok?', then Shipped or Cancelled, and an end state. Placed can retry payment on itself. Mark Cancelled with a bad tone.

Draw a state diagram of a support ticket: Open, In progress, Waiting on customer, Resolved and Closed. Resolved can reopen to In progress. Closed is the end state. Label every transition with a verb phrase.

Edit the existing diagram.json: add a cache node labelled 'Orders cache' (kind cache) that the API reads through (an edge from api to the cache labelled 'reads'), and rename the 'Web app' node to 'Storefront'. Keep everything else unchanged.
